questions.q: Which connective tissue is shown in this slide?
questions.explain: Sparse, thin fibres and scattered cells in an open background are the visible clues.
questions.alt: Whole-mount view of fine thread-like fibres and scattered purple-stained cells on a pale background.

questions.q: How are the fibres arranged in this tissue?
options: Thin and loosely woven in many directions
Thick bundles lying parallel in rows
Thick bundles packed tightly with few cells
Absent, because the tissue is mostly fat cells
questions.explain: The thin thread-like fibres cross the field in all directions with plenty of space between them.
questions.alt: Whole-mount view of fine thread-like fibres and scattered purple-stained cells on a pale background.

questions.q: How does loose connective tissue differ from dense connective tissue?
options: More ground substance and cell types with fewer, thinner fibres
More tightly packed thick collagen bundles
Fewer cells and no ground substance
Fibres arranged only in parallel rows
questions.explain: Loose tissue looks airy because of abundant ground substance; dense tissue is packed with collagen.
questions.alt: Whole-mount view of fine thread-like fibres and scattered purple-stained cells on a pale background.

questions.q: Which connective tissue is shown in this slide?
questions.explain: Packed collagen with few cells and no parallel arrangement points to dense irregular connective tissue.
questions.alt: A thick pink band of collagen runs diagonally between cellular areas with small dark nuclei, with a blood-filled space at the top right.

questions.q: How are the collagen bundles arranged here?
questions.explain: The pink bundles swirl and change direction, which is what 'irregular' refers to.
questions.alt: A thick pink band of collagen runs diagonally between cellular areas with small dark nuclei, with a blood-filled space at the top right.

questions.q: Which sites contain dense irregular connective tissue?
questions.explain: Bundles running in many directions resist stress from several directions, as in dermis and capsules.
questions.alt: A thick pink band of collagen runs diagonally between cellular areas with small dark nuclei, with a blood-filled space at the top right.

questions.q: Which tissue is shown in this slide?
questions.explain: Concentric ring systems around central openings are osteons, the building units of compact bone.
questions.alt: Orange-brown to pale yellow ground section packed with concentric ring systems and bright blue-white holes.

questions.q: What does each ring-shaped unit represent?
options: An osteon: concentric lamellae around a Haversian canal
A trabecula with marrow on each side
A cluster of chondrocytes in a lacuna group
questions.explain: Each osteon has concentric lamellae around a central canal carrying vessels and nerves.
questions.alt: Orange-brown to pale yellow ground section packed with concentric ring systems and bright blue-white holes.

questions.q: Why is this not cancellous bone?
options: It is built from osteons, not trabeculae with marrow spaces
It is made of elastic fibres
questions.explain: Cancellous bone has plates and struts with marrow between them; osteons mark compact bone.
questions.alt: Orange-brown to pale yellow ground section packed with concentric ring systems and bright blue-white holes.
